messages:
hannah: Quick q — we're finalizing the per-route quota contract for /v1/generate. Do we commit to route-level soft-bursts counting only against the route bucket (and signaling the global bucket in headers), or should soft-bursts ever return a 429?

hannah: Proposed header shape we discussed in the doc so far:
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Route-Remaining: 0
X-Route-Limit: 100
X-Route-Burst-Capacity: 20
X-Global-Remaining: 512
X-Global-Limit: 1000
Retry-After: 30
```

raj: I think we originally wanted `-remaining`/`-limit` to match existing semantics. Can we avoid inventing new suffixes like `-bucket`? :thinking_face:

oliver: pinging @katie for SDK expectations — browsers and proxies sometimes normalise or drop custom headers. Prefer `x-rate-limit-*` lowercase to be safe?

katie: SDK note: JS + Python clients already expect `x-rate-limit-*` lowercase and then we map -> rateLimit object. If we add different names we need a migration layer. Also, clients rely on `retry-after` being present for 429s.

omar: SRE perspective: include both route and global signals. Important: clients should prefer route-level backoff when present, otherwise they see weird throttling across routes during spikes. Also suggest including a short human-readable `warning` field in the body for observability.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rate-limit-headers -> canary 2026-03-18T04:30Z :robot_face:

hannah: For backward compat let's emit both sets but keep naming stable. Proposal: `x-rate-limit-route-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-route-limit`, and `x-rate-limit-global-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-global-limit`. Avoid `-burst` field unless we need to expose internal pool buckets.

raj: One more behavioral question: when soft-burst is used, do we return 200 with a body flag like `soft_burst_applied: true`, or return 429? We debated returning soft-429 earlier and I'm concerned about SDK noise.

katie: SDKs prefer deterministic 429s for hard limits. For soft-burst we should avoid 429s. Suggested pattern: return 200 with header `x-soft-burst-used: 1` (or `x-soft-burst-remaining`) plus a small `warning` in the body. Client libraries will surface it as a non-fatal warning.

oliver: To keep semantics simple: status codes == hard failures, headers == signals. So soft-burst = 200 + header signal + body warning. 429 only for global or route hard exhaustion.

hannah: That works. I'll update the spec and add a test vector showing 200+soft-burst and 429+hard-route-fail. @katie can you add the SDK mapping changes (lowercase `x-rate-limit-*` -> rateLimit.route/global) and a migration note?

katie: Yep, I'll update the JS/Python mappers and add a changelog entry. Also will add a small unit test verifying the header parse.

raj: Code-review ping to @hannah and @katie: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4327 — includes the header normalization and test vectors.

hannah: Thanks all. I'll land after tests/CI green. :thumbsup:
